news.title: The Week in Numbers: major oil loss, the future of ice cream
news.summary:
VIDEO SHOWS: n/a

STORY: From major global oil loss to the future of ice cream...this is the Week in Numbers. 

:: Week in Numbers 

:: 2.6 billion 

2.6 billion barrels is the amount of oil the world has lost since the start of the Iran war.

That’s according to the head of Saudi Aramco.

Pre-war global oil demand sat at 103 million barrels per day, meaning the conflict erased a massive 25 days of global consumption.

But are global oil stocks enough to offset what could become the biggest supply disruption on record?

The answer is far from clear, depending not only on how much oil remains in storage, but also on how much of it can actually be released.

For now, most analysts believe the daily supply gap to cover demand amounts to 5 million barrels. 

:: 4.8%

4.8% was how far above historic July peaks last month’s temperature topped in Western Europe. 

Analysts think the region's economy has been hit for hundreds of billions of euros this summer…

With record breaking heat and droughts in the region.

Analysts warn that this is just the beginning, with costs due to rise faster than temperatures.

Climate is changing faster in Europe than on any other continent.

And the damage stretches public finances, redraws the tourism map and could set off wild swings in inflation.

:: 2030

2030 is the year Ford aims to start moving production of some Lincoln models from China back to the U.S. 

That’s what the automaker’s CEO told Reuters Wednesday.

Autos correspondent Nora Eckert said Ford has been preparing this move for some time. 

“This is a substantial move for Ford, as it faces pretty hefty tariffs under the Trump administration. One of its Lincoln models, the Nautilus, had about 52.5% tariffs that it had been facing for the last year.”

Ford said the move was difficult but necessary to strengthen the U.S. auto manufacturing base.

:: 1.5%

1.5% was the year-on-year dip in June U.S. ice cream sales, research data found. 

But manufacturers see little sign that consumers are abandoning ice cream altogether.

Chief Companies Correspondent Alex Marrow said instead, companies are reshaping these products due to pivots in customer demand. 

“So, as more and more consumers are taking weight loss drugs, GLP-1 drugs, as they're also known, we wanted to look at how this is affecting the way people are eating food. We know that it suppresses appetites. But specifically with the hot weather, we looked at ice cream…And essentially it comes down to reducing the number of calories that you put in a serving size.”

Ice cream makers are betting that shoppers will continue to indulge, provided treats come with fewer calories, more protein and simpler ingredient lists.

This shift reflects the industry's broader challenge as eating habits redefine what consumers expect from indulgent foods.

:: 1,500

Over 1,500 Mexican soldiers and National Guard personnel were deployed to the nation’s top avocado-producing region.

That was after the U.S. suspended export inspections there over safety concerns.

This pause is the latest disruption to the region's lucrative avocado trade tied to such concerns for U.S. inspectors. 

Days on, the U.S. embassy said the government would partially restart activities there.
